title: Finite Boolean model preference by minimized predicate extension

historical_origin.author: John McCarthy
historical_origin.note: A finite propositional model-order fragment of circumscription, NOT an implementation of second-order predicate circumscription or original McCarthy's entire AI system.

semantics.input: width n (1..8), distinct satisfying Boolean assignments of a previously evaluated theory (bit masks 0..2^n-1), designated minimized predicate mask M and fixed predicate mask F; M & F=0
semantics.output: ordered finite set of exactly all preferred entire satisfying assignments (numeric ascending), or explicit NO-MODELS when input has no satisfying assignments
semantics.dominance: u strictly dominates v iff (u & F)=(v & F), ((u & M) & (v & M))=(u & M), and (u & M)!=(v & M). Positions outside M|F are variable without affecting comparison.
semantics.inclusion: keep v iff no other satisfying u strictly dominates it
semantics.boundary: Minimize set inclusion of true minimized atoms, NOT numeric value, number of true bits, edit distance, confidence or arbitrary heuristic rank.
semantics.absence: 0 satisfying models means NO-MODELS, and must not be misreported as a true skeptical proposition by vacuous universal quantification.
semantics.epistemic: Output is a defeasible model preference, not an OBSERVATION, mathematical certainty about the physical world, or destructive update of D9 truth maintenance.
semantics.scope: Ground propositional finite and explicit-model input; no first-order quantifier elimination, hidden open-world completion, or default rule engine.

examples.label: incomparable abnormalities
examples.why: 1 and 2 are distinct incomparable minimal exceptions; 3 contains both and is dominated

examples.label: cardinality is not subset minimality
examples.why: 3 has two bits and 4 one bit yet neither abnormality set is subset of the other

examples.label: fixed world signatures remain distinct
examples.why: fixed bit 2 differs, so the two worlds must never dominate each other

examples.label: variable (nonminimized) predicates do not suppress alternatives
examples.why: 0 and 2 have same minimal abnormality, both survive; 3 has abnormal bit and is dominated

examples.label: contradiction explicit
examples.why: inconsistent theory has no world; not a proof of every proposition

examples.label: nonmonotonic update example
examples.why: later hard evidence that bit0 is true leaves only model 1 and withdraws prior default that bit0 was absent

nearby_existing.behavioral_distinction: JTMS/ATMS justify or retract facts under specific assumptions; abductive reasoning seeks explaining hypotheses; Bayes ranks weighted hypotheses; circumscription prefers models by subset order of designated minimized predicates with FIXED/VARYING boundary and returns all incomparable preferred models.

crossdomain.mapping: Prefer knowledge worlds with the smallest extension of explicitly designated abnormality atoms.
Hypothesis diagnosis: minimize failed-component atoms while conditioning on fixed measurements; not a driver or assertion of physical diagnosis.
Model anomalous sensor or sky-observation assumptions while preserving multiple incomparable explanations; no astrophysical empirical claim.
Grammar exception hypotheses can be treated as minimized exception atoms, but linguistic derivations themselves remain separate and unvalidated.
